principle.name: DRY - Don't Repeat Yourself (Architectural Level)
principle.description: Eliminate architectural duplication through shared patterns and components
principle.rationale: Duplicated architecture increases maintenance burden and inconsistency

example.scenario: Multiple modules implementing similar communication patterns
example.bad: Implement similar patterns independently in each module

principle.name: SOLID - Single Responsibility (Architectural Level)
principle.description: Each module/component should have one reason to change

example.scenario: A module that handles UI, business logic, and persistence
example.good: Split into separate UI, business logic, and persistence modules
example.bad: Keep all concerns in one monolithic module

example.scenario: Business logic directly depends on database implementation
example.good: Business logic depends on repository interface
example.bad: Business logic directly calls database functions

principle.name: LEAN - Eliminate Architectural Waste
principle.description: Remove unnecessary layers, abstractions, and complexity
principle.rationale: Waste increases cognitive load and development time

example.good: Remove unused modules and simplify abstractions
example.bad: Keep "future-proof" architecture that adds no value

principle.name: KISS - Keep It Simple, Stupid (Architectural Level)
principle.description: Prefer simple architectures over complex ones
principle.rationale: Complexity is the enemy of maintainability

example.good: Use modular monolith for simple applications
example.bad: Over-engineer with microservices when not needed

guidelines.guideline: Each module should have a single, well-defined purpose
Separate presentation, business logic, and data access
Dependencies should flow inward (higher layers depend on lower layers)
Use dependency injection for loose coupling
Use patterns that solve actual problems, not for their own sake
Document why each pattern was chosen
Be willing to remove patterns that no longer serve their purpose
Document the context, decision, and consequences
